kept.excerpt: Anthropic does not plan to release an internal model they're calling "Model 2" that appears to be more powerful than top-of-the-line Mythos, but the company is not slowing development broadly, according to its latest risk report. "As part of our standard R&D process, we internally train and evaluate many different exploratory versions of models that we don't intend to release. Model 2 is one of these," the company told Axios.
kept.relevance: Provides a company statement close to the experiment cutoff that a stronger internal model had no planned external release, while distinguishing continued development from public availability.

kept.excerpt: The company stated at the time that one of the breaches was carried out by an unreleased LLM. Its new risk report reveals that it has developed two successors to Claude Mythos 5 dubbed Model 1 and Model 2. The latter algorithm, which is the more capable of the two, is “heavily used” by Anthropic staffers.
kept.relevance: Corroborates the existence of successor models while identifying their use as internal rather than evidence of a qualifying public launch.

kept.excerpt: We shared our August 2026 Risk Report. Our Risk Reports aim to provide a direct, candid, and informative description of how we see the risks of our systems and our state of preparedness for them (particularly the catastrophic risks addressed in our Responsible Scaling Policy). It covers the risks of Anthropic's models and actions between our previous February 2026 risk report and the report's coverage date of July 15, as well as our mitigations for those risks and our forward-looking plans in each category.
kept.publisher: Anthropic — Responsible Scaling Policy, dated August 14 update
kept.relevance: Verifies the official publication date and July 15 coverage boundary of the risk report underlying the recent successor-model reporting.

kept.excerpt: Claude Opus 5 is available today. It’s a thoughtful and proactive model that comes close to the frontier intelligence of Claude Fable 5 at half the price. On coding and knowledge work evaluations like Frontier-Bench and GDPval-AA, Opus 5 is the new state-of-the-art, though it remains behind Mythos 5 on cybersecurity tasks.
kept.relevance: Documents a recent public model release and its official positioning relative to Fable and Mythos, which matters because a new Claude release must also meet the question's naming or class-description requirement.

kept.excerpt: As of today, June 30, the export controls on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 have been lifted. Fable 5 will be available starting tomorrow, Wednesday, July 1, to users globally on the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork. We have also restored access to Mythos 5 for a set of US organizations, following the US government’s approval on June 26.
kept.relevance: Establishes the restored public-access baseline for the existing Fable 5 and shows that Mythos 5 access remained restricted, while documenting regulatory friction affecting releases.

kept.excerpt: Today we’re launching Claude Fable 5: a Mythos-class model that we’ve made safe for general use. With more capable models arriving in the coming months, we’re working to improve our safeguards and reduce false positives as quickly as we can. Claude Fable 5 is available everywhere today. Claude Mythos 5 is restricted to Glasswing partners (with cyber safeguards lifted) and soon to select biology researchers (with biology and chemistry safeguards lifted) only, until our broader trusted access program is available.
kept.relevance: Defines the starting Mythos-class public release, distinguishes it from restricted Mythos access, and supplies Anthropic's contemporaneous broad indication that more capable models were expected in the coming months.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-08-18, interpreted using the question's ET convention. Included six items with verifiable publication dates or explicitly dated official update sections on or before the cutoff. Dates were checked against fetched publisher metadata, visible datelines, and dated official sections; the Axios syndication visibly identifies August 14, 2026, and its original Axios URL independently carries the same date. web_fetch failed because of a provider-configuration error, so full-page checks used the agent-reach skill's read-only web channel. The official August risk-report PDF could not be retrieved through that channel; its dated official publication notice and contemporaneous reporting were retained instead. Excerpts use only the relevant dated article bodies or update sections; later navigation, recommendations, and current product-page content were excluded. Sources showing later revisions or lacking a reliable publication date were excluded, as were prediction-market pages, odds, market prices, and post-cutoff reporting. The evidence pack does not assert an outcome, and these live URLs are citations rather than archived snapshots.
